L0@P0: GLOBAL PLURIPOTENTIAL THEORY OVER A TRIVIALLY VALUED
L1@P0: FIELD
L2@P0: SEBASTIEN BOUCKSOM AND MATTIAS JONSSON ´
L3@P0: Dedicated to Ahmed Zeriahi for all his contributions to complex analysis and geometry
L4@P0: Abstract. We develop global pluripotential theory in the setting of Berkovich geometry
L5@P0: over a trivially valued field. Specifically, we define and study functions and measures of
L6@P0: finite energy and the non-Archimedean Monge–Amp`ere operator on any (possibly reducible)
L7@P0: projective variety. We also investigate the topology of the space of valuations of linear
L8@P0: growth, and the behavior of psh functions thereon.

L36@P1: Introduction
L37@P1: The main purpose of the present paper is to lay the foundations of pluripotential theory
L38@P1: in the setting of Berkovich geometry over a trivially valued field, paralleling as much as
L39@P1: possible the known theory in the complex analytic case.
L40@P1: Pluripotential theory is a crucial tool in complex analysis and geometry, and A. Zeriahi has
L41@P1: been a central protagonist in the story of its development. For an excellent introduction, see
L42@P1: the book by V. Guedj and A. Zeriahi [GZ17]. This theory lies at the heart of the variational
L43@P1: approach to complex Monge–Amp`ere equations [BBGZ13], which proved particularly fruitful
L44@P1: in relation to K¨ahler–Einstein metrics, and ultimately led to a new proof of the Yau–Tian–
L45@P1: Donaldson (YTD) conjecture for Fano manifolds [BBJ21], later generalized to (log terminal)
L46@P1: Fano varieties [LTW19, Li19].
L47@P1: There are several reasons for developing a corresponding theory over a trivially valued
L48@P1: field, that is, any field equipped with the trivial (non-Archimedean) valuation. First, the
L49@P1: Berkovich approach to non-Archimedean geometry is the one closest to the complex analytic intuition, and it is natural to see to what extent the complex analytic theory admits
L50@P1: a counterpart in the setting of Berkovich spaces. Second, Berkovich spaces over a trivially or discretely valued field can often be used to study degenerations in complex geometry [FJ05a, FJ05b, FJ07, FJ11, BoJ17, BHJ19, Shi19], and such degenerations are central
L51@P1: to the variational approach to the YTD conjecture [BBJ21, Li20], through the notion of
L52@P1: geodesic rays.
L53@P1: The thrust of the YTD conjecture is to relate the existence of a solution to a non-linear
L54@P1: PDE to an algebro-geometric condition known as K-stability, which has recently also come
L55@P1: to play a key role in the study of moduli spaces, especially for Fano varieties. [ABHX20,
L56@P1: BHLX21, BLX19, LXZ21, XZ20]. The relation of K-stability with spaces of valuations and
L57@P1: non-Archimedean geometry over trivially valued fields, originally pointed out in [BHJ17], is
L58@P1: one major motivation to endeavor the present study, and will be further exploited in the
L59@P1: companion papers [BoJ21, BoJ22].

L61@P1: condition phrased in terms of Gm-equivariant degenerations (X ,L) → A
